subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: The three per-format DETERMINATIONS are each implemented at their own call site and read correct. (a) format 1 `all of the operands in the statement`: CheckComposite("SUBTRACT", minuends, recv) superimposes the sending operands AND the identifier-2 receivers. (b) format 2 `excluding the data item that follow the word GIVING`: CheckComposite("SUBTRACT", [minuends, fromX], []) passes an EMPTY receiver list - pinned by the spec-derived golden conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/ca4_giving_composite, whose SUBTRACT leg (`SUBTRACT B FROM D GIVING C` over 25-digit operands and a 16-digit GIVING receiver) is legal only because the receiver is excluded. (c) format 3 `the two corresponding operands for each separate pair`: the check runs inside CorrMatch's per-pair loop with exactly [source] + [target]. The rule's `when native arithmetic is in effect` antecedent is honoured at StatementValidation.cs:107 (`if (data.Options.Arithmetic != ArithmeticMode.Native) return true`) - confirmed by k1/k2, where a composite far past the cap compiles under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. 14.7.7 rule 2b's exclusions ride InComposite (binary-char/-short/-long/-double and float usages) and OfExpr's silence on function-call operands, so an intrinsic-function operand contributes nothing. The 31-digit CAP itself is 14.7.7 rule 2's row, not this one; this row is only the per-format determination.
